archetypes.name: bash-flow
archetypes.rationale: Diff changes many Bash failure paths where set -e, captured rc values, process substitution, and sourced helpers can silently change behavior.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate Bash control flow, especially branches that temporarily disable errexit, commands inside command substitutions, process substitutions, and functions sourced into larger scripts. Check whether new rc capture, local variable use, and return/exit behavior preserve the existing stdout KV contracts on every failure path. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: fd-routing
archetypes.rationale: The feature depends on surfacing stderr tails from subprocess scopes whose fd2 is often redirected or quiet-mode remapped.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace stderr-tail emission from producers through the actual caller scopes that reach operator chat. Pay particular attention to quiet-mode FD 3/4 behavior, subprocess redirects, tee process substitutions, and cases where emitting inside a child would only write to a capture file. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: tail-redaction
archetypes.rationale: The diff expands failure-output surfacing and must not leak raw sidecars, tmp paths, tokens, or stale tail content.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review every new stderr-tail write and emit path for redaction and source selection. Confirm callers emit only bounded redacted tail artifacts, do not cat raw wrapper logs, respect the disable knob, and avoid stale or wrong-source tail clobbering. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: ci-waterfall
archetypes.rationale: ship-pr changes thread LAUNCHER_EXIT, output stems, rollback, and early-return behavior through a complex CI recovery state machine.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the CI fix and recovery waterfall changes as state-machine transitions. Verify the correct output stem is used at each tier, launcher stdout parsing cannot mask failures, rollback happens before continuing, and early returns still preserve the intended escalation semantics. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: cleanup-retention
archetypes.rationale: Cleanup retention semantics changed from top-level mtime to bounded nested activity with fail-safe find handling.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the cleanup retention implementation and docs as a coherent contract. Check the find predicates, maxdepth boundary, symlink handling, tmp file versus directory behavior, enumeration failure behavior, and whether tests accurately pin the intended deletion and retention cases. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: fixture-isolation
archetypes.rationale: Large harness additions use copied helper scripts, PATH stubs, env overrides, and sourced production scripts that can create false positives or host coupling.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the new regression harness fixtures for hermeticity and realistic coverage. Look for missing copied dependencies, reliance on host-specific tools or paths, leaked environment variables between cases, stubs that do not exercise the production branch claimed, and assertions that can pass for the wrong reason. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
